fields.label: Session Key
fields.description: The sshd child process that handled this connection, scoped by boot id where journald supplies one. sshd's own correlation identifier, so grouping on it is a grouping rather than a guess.

fields.label: Status
fields.description: Unknown means opened, never closed, and too old to still be running. Deliberately not Closed: an sshd that was killed, a host that lost power and a log that stopped being ingested all look like this, and none of them is the user logging out.

fields.label: Auth Method
fields.description: Free text, never an enum: password, publickey, keyboard-interactive/pam, gssapi-with-mic and others all appear.

fields.label: Key Fingerprint
fields.description: Only recorded when sshd runs at LogLevel VERBOSE. Below that, which key was used cannot be answered afterwards.

fields.label: Attribution Method
fields.options:
Audit Session
User and Time
Ambiguous
Unattributed
fields.description: How the sudo commands were tied to this session. Audit Session is exact — PAM stamps every process in a login with the same id. User and Time is inferred from the actor and the session window, which is usually right and is not the same kind of fact. Ambiguous means more than one session fitted and nothing was attributed.

fields.label: Audit Session
fields.description: PAM's login session id. When present it makes sudo attribution exact; it is absent on hosts whose auth records come from auth.log rather than journald.

fields.label: Last Seen
fields.description: The last event of any kind belonging to this session. Not a logout time — it is the last evidence the session existed, and it is how far command attribution reaches for a session that was never seen closing.
